paper.title_en: Cryogenic pure CsI read out by SiPM for CE\(\nu\)NS: Enhanced light yield and anti-quenching dynamics
paper.abstract_en: Coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CE<math altimg="si11.svg" display="inline" id="d1e533"><mi>ν</mi></math>NS) represents a powerful probe for low-energy neutrino physics. In this work, we present a novel cryogenic detection scheme utilizing pure CsI crystals coupled with silicon photomultiplier (SiPM) readout. While previous experiments have demonstrated the viability of this detector architecture at liquid-nitrogen temperatures (77 K), theoretical models anticipate significant performance enhancements at deeper cryogenic temperatures. To systematically investigate this regime, we developed a custom-built cryogenic facility with continuous temperature regulation from 30 K to 293 K. Building upon prior single-photon calibrations of the SiPMs at 40 K, we characterized the pure CsI detection system using 13.9–59.54 keV X/<math altimg="si41.svg" display="inline" id="d1e538"><mi>γ</mi></math>-rays and 5.5 MeV <math altimg="si43.svg" display="inline" id="d1e543"><mi>α</mi></math>-particles. Crucially, we report the observation of a pronounced anti-quenching phenomenon. At 35 K, the scintillation light yield for densely ionizing <math altimg="si43.svg" display="inline" id="d1e549"><mi>α</mi></math>-particles reaches 19.2 p.e./keV, unambiguously exceeding the 17.3 p.e./keV measured for electron recoils induced by <math altimg="si41.svg" display="inline" id="d1e554"><mi>γ</mi></math>-rays. Because the ionization density profiles of <math altimg="si43.svg" display="inline" id="d1e559"><mi>α</mi></math>-particles closely emulate those of low-energy nuclear recoils generated via CE<math altimg="si11.svg" display="inline" id="d1e564"><mi>ν</mi></math>NS, this enhanced light yield for high linear energy transfer (LET) interactions is of paramount importance for validating the reliability of this technique. This cryogenic pure CsI platform offers a transformative pathway for achieving the ultra-low thresholds required in next-generation reactor CE<math altimg="si11.svg" display="inline" id="d1e570"><mi>ν</mi></math>NS experiments.
